tools.name: add_kit_sounds
tools.description: Add the user's own list of sounds to a kit (an app's or a game's events: names, optional moments and lengths), or a ready set's events with its library sounds already in use. Names, keys, order and lengths stay the user's; SFXMint writes how each sounds. Without kit_id it starts a new kit for the list. Free (no generation). Then call fill_kit_from_library to use free library sounds first, and make only the gaps.

kit_id.description: Add to this kit (kit_…); leave out to start a new kit.

sounds.description: The sounds, in the user's order.

name.description: The event, e.g. 'Ride request' or 'Coin pickup'.

scene.description: The scene heading from the user's list or approved proposal (optional); matching existing scene names are reused.

seconds.description: Length in seconds, 0.2 to 10 (optional; rounded to the nearest a kit offers).

key.description: The user's own event key or file name, e.g. '01-lab-air' (optional).

set.description: Instead of sounds: a ready set's id from get_sound_set (its events, with its library sounds in use).

tools.name: change_kit_take
tools.description: Change a kit sound's take as it is, free: say what is off in the user's words (change, any language) or name the action. Three versions come back as new takes of the sound (a light, medium and strong change; for a loop, three seamless loops of 12-14 s for a steady sound), with file links; the take in use stays until pick_kit_take. No generation is used and no plan is needed. When the words ask for a different sound rather than a change to this one, it answers no_action with the writer's description: the user can make that at kit_url. Let the user listen and pick one.

kit_id.description: The kit id from start_game_kit or add_kit_sounds (kit_…).

take_id.description: The take to change (default: the sound's take in use).

change.description: What is off, in the user's words: 'too muddy', 'make it loop', 'sounds too close'.

action.description: crisper: too muddy; heavier: too light; shorter_tail: rings on too long; longer_tail: stops too abruptly; room: too dry; far: too close; loop: make it loop

tools.name: change_sound
tools.description: Change one take of a generation this account made, from the take itself: say what is off in the user's words (change, any language) or name the action. Three versions come back (a light, medium and strong change; for a loop, three seams) as CC0 WAV files. Free: no generation is used and no plan is needed. When the words ask for a different sound rather than a change to this one, it answers no_action with a description to pass to generate_sound. The user should listen and pick one.

order_id.description: The generation, from generate_sound or get_generation

change.description: What is off, in the user's words: 'too muddy', 'make it loop', 'sounds too close'

action.description: crisper: too muddy; heavier: too light; shorter_tail: rings on too long; longer_tail: stops too abruptly; room: too dry; far: too close; loop: make it loop

tools.name: export_game_kit
tools.description: What to put in the project: every included sound's event key and the take in use (file link valid 15 minutes, SHA-256), the sounds not ready yet, and zip_url for one ZIP (download it with the same Authorization header) holding the files in the chosen format, sounds.json (event key → file) and a README. Wire the game's events to sounds.json and let the user check the sounds in the game.

kit_id.description: The kit id from start_game_kit or add_kit_sounds (kit_…).

format.description: File type in the ZIP (default wav).

tools.name: fill_kit_from_library
tools.description: Fill a kit's sounds from the free CC0 library first: each sound without a take is searched by its name and length, and a full match becomes its take in use, free. Answers what matched (let the user listen), the nearest sounds for others (use_library_sound to use one) and the gaps to make with make_kit_sounds.

kit_id.description: The kit id from start_game_kit or add_kit_sounds (kit_…).

sound_ids.description: Only these sounds (default: every sound without a take).

tools.name: find_kit_sound_candidates
tools.description: Up to five free library sounds for one kit sound, by its name or your own words, with their length, character and a listening URL. Nothing changes until use_library_sound.

kit_id.description: The kit id from start_game_kit or add_kit_sounds (kit_…).

tools.name: generate_sound
tools.description: Make a new sound effect from a description when the library has nothing suitable (search_sounds has no full match and its closest sounds do not suit; it then returns generate_available). Needs an SFXMint API key and a pass or plan on the account — a 24-hour pass ($3.90, 50 sounds) or a plan (from $9.90 for 30 days, 50 to 200 a day); the 3 free tries are on the website only — each up to 4 CC0 WAV takes of up to 10 s; one that makes no take does not count; without a plan it answers payment_required with buy_url and website_url (the website's page where the user can make it and hear it first). Returns CC0 WAV files (signed links valid 15 minutes) with SHA-256 and seed; if they are not ready within about 25 seconds, it returns the order id for get_generation. AI-generated: the user should listen before use.

prompt.description: The sound the user needs, in plain words and any language: what it is for and what should be heard. With enhance (recommended), SFXMint writes the description the model gets. Leave out lengths (use duration_s).

duration_s.description: Longest length in seconds. Leave it out and SFXMint chooses from the description; either way the silence before and after the sound is cut, so a take can be shorter

variations.description: How many takes to make (default 4; one generation either way)

enhance.description: Recommended: SFXMint writes the prompt into the description the model gets, as the website's AI Enhance does, and the result gives that description. Default false: the prompt goes to the model exactly as written.

tools.name: get_game_kit
tools.description: A Game kit's state: its scenes, its sounds (event key, when it plays, status, the takes made with short-lived file links, SHA-256 and length, and the take in use), how its makes are paid (the account's plan's generations of the day, or the plan it needs) and next_step. Needs the API key that started the kit.

kit_id.description: The kit id from start_game_kit or add_kit_sounds (kit_…).

tools.name: get_generation
tools.description: Check a generation started with generate_sound or change_sound: status, and fresh download links for the finished takes.

tools.name: get_role_sound
tools.description: Choose this when the task calls for a sound for a named event or interaction — a button click, purchase success, error beep, level-up, dialogue blip, notification. Pass the role as plain words: role ids (click, success, purchase-success, dialogue-blip, notification…) and common aliases (button click, ka-ching, jump scare, text blip…) are all accepted. Returns a qualified candidate for that role when one satisfies the requested constraints, with MP3/WAV URLs, 2-3 alternates and the family page for browsing more. Five core game roles include content_check (verified/unverified/rejected), scoped to scene, role, format and exact file SHA256; unverified previews are not certified suitable. Download selected files locally and retain originals. Task-permitted processing requires a recipe, output SHA256, renewed file checks and a listening check; changed bytes do not inherit content review. Other task-permitted sources or local synthesis may be mixed in. Optional style: crisp (short, bright, dry), soft (darker, gentler), spacious (reverb, longer tail), balanced (default: most typical). For multiple events consider get_sound_set; use search_sounds for a description or a gap. These are task branches, not a fixed sequence. Unknown roles return not_found with the full role list; GET https://sfxmint.com/api/v1/roles lists roles with aliases.

role.description: Role id or alias, e.g. 'click', 'button click', 'purchase-success', 'ka-ching', 'error beep', 'level-up', 'dialogue blip', 'notification'

style.description: Optional. balanced (default) = the family's most typical take; crisp = short, bright, dry; soft = darker, gentler; spacious = reverb, longer tail

max_duration_ms.description: Hard maximum delivered duration in milliseconds.

loop.description: Require prepared loop metadata; seam evidence is returned separately.

tools.name: get_sound
tools.description: Get full metadata for one sound by slug, including download URLs, description and measured acoustics (attack/tail/brightness + character labels).

tools.name: get_sound_set
tools.description: Get a coherent set of sounds for an app or game in one call — one sound per role, with format metadata, hashes and stable download URLs. Use it when the task needs a whole kit; use get_role_sound for one event. Check content_check: verified/unverified/rejected is bound to the exact role, format and file SHA256; unverified files still require listening in context. Sets include UI styles, game and app scenarios, acoustic-drum-kit, animal-calls (15 isolated calls), and dungeon-traps (6 isolated mechanisms).

format.description: File format for selection and checks (default WAV; OGG only among sounds published before 2026-10-14). Legacy urls remains MP3; download_urls follows this format.

set.description: Set id (default ui-crisp). Includes acoustic-drum-kit, animal-calls and dungeon-traps alongside the UI and scenario sets listed in the enum.

tools.name: list_kit_sounds
tools.description: List the sounds of a Game kit's scenes, free: after start_game_kit planned the scenes, show them to the user, then call this with the scenes to keep (all by default; the others are switched off). Call get_game_kit after about 15 seconds.

kit_id.description: The kit id from start_game_kit or add_kit_sounds (kit_…).

scene_ids.description: Scene ids to list (default: every scene).

tools.name: make_kit_sounds
tools.description: Make sounds in a Game kit: each sound gets up to four takes, and each sound made is one generation. Each uses one of the account's plan generations of the day, shared with generate_sound; nothing is charged. Without a plan it answers payment_required with buy_url, and when the day's are used with plans_url: the user chooses a plan on that page (a 24-hour pass for $3.90 (50 sounds), or a plan from $9.90 for 30 days: 50 to 200 generations a day for the whole account), never the agent.

kit_id.description: The kit id from start_game_kit or add_kit_sounds (kit_…).

sound_ids.description: Sounds to make or remake (default: every listed sound not made yet).

tools.name: pick_kit_take
tools.description: Use one of a sound's takes in the kit (the first take is used until the user picks). Let the user listen to the takes first.

kit_id.description: The kit id from start_game_kit or add_kit_sounds (kit_…).

tools.name: search_sounds
tools.description: Free-text search over the SFXMint library of free CC0 sound effects. Use it for sound descriptions, additional constraints or gaps left by another tool. Choose get_role_sound for a named event or get_sound_set for multiple events when that fits the task; these are task branches, not a fixed sequence. Hard constraints (duration, loop, format, excluded words) always apply. results hold sounds whose text has every word of the query. When there are none, closest lists the nearest sounds that meet every hard constraint, best first, each with missing_terms: judge them from title and description and let the user listen. library_fit says how well the library covers the request (full, close, weak, none); anything short of full also returns generation options. Returns direct, hotlinkable MP3/WAV URLs and verified OGG (Vorbis) URLs where available — no API key, no attribution required — plus measured acoustics (attack_ms, tail_ms, centroid_hz), character labels like 'bright · punchy · tight', loop/file-QC status, and score/match as ranking evidence only (role = known role default, exact = all words hit, partial = some words hit, semantic = nearest by meaning).

query.description: Keywords or a natural-language description, e.g. 'door slam', 'soft UI confirmation chime', 'coin pickup'

category.description: Optional category slug: ui, retro-game, transition, impact, ambience, water, fire-electric, footsteps, door, mechanical, paper-fabric, glass, animal, crowd, cartoon, magic-scifi, horror, feedback, instrument, office, human, vehicle, household

max_duration_ms.description: Hard maximum delivered duration in milliseconds; format-specific measurement is required.

loop.description: Require (true) or exclude (false) a candidate marked with prepared loop metadata; seam evidence is returned separately.

format.description: Delivery format (ogg = Ogg Vorbis, only sounds published before 2026-10-14 have it); loop=true defaults to WAV when omitted.

tools.name: start_game_kit
tools.description: Start a Game kit: SFXMint plans the sounds one game needs and makes them as CC0 takes to pick from — the same project the user sees on the website. Use it when the user wants sounds for a whole game or scene and the library (get_sound_set, get_role_sound) does not cover them. Needs an SFXMint API key. Planning and listing are free; each sound made uses one of the account's plan generations of the day (a 24-hour pass for $3.90 (50 sounds), or a plan from $9.90 for 30 days: 50 to 200 generations a day for the whole account), which the user buys in the browser: without a plan nothing is made (see get_game_kit). Returns kit_id and kit_url; call get_game_kit after about 15 seconds.

game.description: What the game is and what the player does, in a few sentences (genre, setting, main actions). For one scene, what happens in it.

feel_text.description: More words on the feel, e.g. 'soft, warm' (optional).

avoid.description: What the sounds should leave out, e.g. 'voices, music' (optional).

one_scene.description: true: list 3–6 sounds for one scene at once; making them needs a plan, like generate_sound. Default false: plan the whole game's scenes first.

tools.name: use_library_sound
tools.description: Use a library sound (its slug) as a take of a kit sound, free. It becomes the take in use when the sound has none; otherwise it waits beside the others for the user to compare.

kit_id.description: The kit id from start_game_kit or add_kit_sounds (kit_…).
